claim_ceiling: The query-map MVP ships a verified progressive user-visible slice: one bounded upstream OpenCaseLaw page (enforced budget_max=1, observed network_calls=1) yields a complete, valid, source-linked bundle with a clickable map in ~4-6 s cold and ~0.15 s warm; the wider multi-channel retrieval and the source-constrained generative answer run as pollable jobs that never block the browser; already-rendered geometry is preserved exactly (points_moved=0 and points_displaced_by_refit=0 in both the producer artifact and the auditor's own run); the answer cites only bundle decisions; the independent adversarial counter-authority pass is grounded verbatim in the retrieved text; all of it runs on free models against a public, key-free source. Recomputed live by the auditor in one true-cold run and one full end-to-end run, with 19/19 sampled and cited decision ids resolving to real OpenCaseLaw decisions. NOT claimed: legal usefulness of the 2-D projection (still a query-conditioned TF-IDF+SVD+KMeans baseline, 118/194 decisions in one cluster, fragmentary TF-IDF labels), external citation-service validation (the product's strict_local validator marks every cited id 'unverified' because api_base is null), validation of prose-embedded citation tokens, the single-language character of the first-drawn map, or the comparative map-vs-list human gate (human_gate_ready=false, only a real owner/jurist session can pass it).

advisory_annotations: F1 (minor, provenance): the '288 concurrent /api/health probes ... 7 citations' sentence in reports/product/CYCLE_38665681083.md section 1 and in state/product.json progressive_slice.negative_result is backed by no artifact and splices two runs - the cycle's own recorded probe counts are 259 (cold), 89 (v2) and 5 (fixture), and the run with 7 citations is v2 with 89 probes. My own drive of the same blocking path measured 299 probes / 0 failures, so the substance is corroborated; persist the baseline drive as an artifact or mark the figures as unpersisted cycle-local observations. Same for the pre-change baseline (136.79 s start, 150.70 s enrich, 136.61 s upstream, 101.69 s model, 49.00 s hydration) quoted as measured in the report, in state/product.json ...progressive_slice.why and in three source docstrings plus two test docstrings; my measurement of the old blocking enrich (146.89 s) corroborates it within ~3%.

F2 (minor, undisclosed limitation): the first page is 38/38 French with a single channel (stages=('search',), lang_max_pages=0, max_requests=1) while the finished map is DE 73 / FR 30 / IT 36 / unknown 47 across five channels. All 38 first-page decisions do survive into the final 194, so the 'real subset of the same retrieval' claim is true, but the report's honest-limits section should say the map drawn first is monolingual in a trilingual court system.

F3 (minor, coverage): all 21 new tests run retrieval_mode='fixture', and _retrieve_first_page in fixture mode bypasses first_page_config() entirely (it replays the whole fixture - 105 decisions - which is why 'assert len(decisions) >= 50' passes trivially). Nothing offline pins the bounded single-request retrieval that is the cycle's central mechanism; one pure-function test on first_page_config(max_requests == 1, stages == ('search',)) would pin it.

F4 (minor, wording): 'the answer is never generated from the partial first-page candidate set' is false when the expansion job errors (_await_expand returns as soon as the job is not 'running', including 'error'); and the UI pill counts 10 counter-authorities (isCounter excludes 'cited') while the bundle and run_status count 16 (any status != 'none').

F5 (observation, pre-existing, outside this diff): the auditor's own live run produced an inline prose token [vd_findinfo_Decision___2013___894] (accented e) that does not byte-match the canonical bundle id vd_findinfo_D_cision___2013___894; the decision is real and grounded and the prose is plain text, but citation_validation (mode strict_local, api_base null) only validates the structured cited_decision_ids and never checks prose tokens.
